questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Eswatini?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Demographics” part of the Eswatini article.

questions.proof: SiSwati and English are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was called Swaziland until April _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Eswatini article.

questions.proof: It was called Swaziland until April 2018.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The two countries that touch it are _____ and South Africa.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “South”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Eswatini article, under the heading “Overview”.

questions.proof: The two countries that touch it are Mozambique and South Africa.
